body:
Source: GitHub issue #1050 (bug, P1-high). Re-verified on main @ de8a130a: packages/rails-guard/bin/rails-guard.mjs:78-99 loads ONE ticket when `--ticket` is given and `resolveRailGlobs(cliRails, ticket)` (lib/rails.mjs:16-29) returns only `ticket.rails`; with neither `--rails` nor `--ticket` the bin exits 1 (`no --rails supplied and no --ticket given`). Rails are frozen for everyone, so a change editing ANOTHER active ticket's frozen rail passes the local P3 gate clean. The CI gate already takes the union: lib/ci/rail-freeze.mjs:144-148 iterates every base-tip ticket, skips `completed === true` (strict boolean), and collects every rail; packages/prosecute/lib/tier.mjs:153-157 does the same and reports `touches rails deny-path of ticket <id>`. Reproduced by the reporter: a lane editing `plugins/adlc-copilot/hooks/test/copilot-io-contract.test.mjs` (a rail of a different active ticket) got `rails-guard --ticket <mine>` exit 0, then `tier-check` promoted the change to TRUST-ROOT for the same edit — the failure arrived late and labelled as tiering.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/rails-guard` is ENFORCEMENT tier (packages/prosecute/lib/tier.mjs ENFORCEMENT_PREFIXES): a clean same-model P5 is not sufficient; the PR needs a signature-verified cross-model attestation recorded by the key-holder (the parent handles that ceremony — your job is to report `tier-check`'s exact `git-change:<base>:<digest>` line and which reviewer family reviewed the final commit). Layout: bin/rails-guard.mjs (imports loadTickets, globMatch, resolveBase, ADLC_DIR from @adlc/core; `--tickets` defaults to `${ADLC_DIR}/tickets.json`, and @adlc/core's loadTickets already reads this repo's sharded store through that path — verify by running the bin in the worktree), lib/rails.mjs (resolveRailGlobs, checkRailEdits), lib/check.mjs (runChecks — rail edits + suppression markers; suppressions are allowed by markers in the TICKET BODY, which is why `--ticket` still matters), lib/output.mjs (formatViolations, buildResult). Rails you must not touch: lib/ci/** (the CI union lives in lib/ci/rail-freeze.mjs — import nothing from it into the bin; the agreement is proven by a test that drives BOTH), lib/suppressions.mjs, lib/version-only.mjs, lib/trust-root-authorization.mjs, bin/rails-guard-ci.mjs, and the ci-*/suppressions-operative/version-only/rail-addition-sanction/trust-root-authorization tests. Tests: `npm test -w packages/rails-guard`. Callers of the local bin to keep working: the issue-lanes flow (`adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <id>`), fleet gate pipelines and plugin docs — `grep -rn "rails-guard --" packages/*/lib plugins/*/ docs/ --include=*.mjs --include=*.md | grep -v rails-guard-ci` before changing any flag semantics.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. ONE exported pure function in lib/rails.mjs, `resolveRailSet({ cliRails, ticket, tickets })`, returns `{ rails: Array<{ glob: string, owner: string|null }>, error: string|null }`: explicit `--rails` globs win (owner null); otherwise the UNION over every ticket in `tickets` whose `completed !== true` (strict boolean, exactly rail-freeze.mjs's rule) of its `rails`, each tagged with the declaring ticket id, de-duplicated by (glob, owner). `--ticket` no longer decides which rails exist. When the union is empty and no `--rails` was given, `error` = `no active ticket declares rails and no --rails supplied — nothing to guard` and the bin exits 1 as today. `resolveRailGlobs` may remain as a thin wrapper or be removed; no caller outside this package imports it (verify).
2. The bin always loads the ticket store (`--tickets` path, default unchanged); `--ticket <id>` is optional, still validated to exist when given, and selects ONLY which ticket's `allow-suppression` declarations apply (runChecks's `ticketBody`) and which id is reported as `ticket` in the result. A run with neither `--ticket` nor `--rails` is legal and checks the union with no suppression allowances.
3. Every `rail-edit` violation gains `ownerTicket: string|null`. `formatViolations` prints `(rail of ticket <id>)` after the glob list when `ownerTicket` is non-null and differs from the `--ticket` id (or when no `--ticket` was given); JSON `violations[].ownerTicket` is always present. `buildResult` gains `railSources: Array<{ glob, owner }>` (the resolved set); `railGlobs` stays the de-duplicated string list for compatibility.
4. Regression guards: exit codes unchanged (0 / 1 / 2); a change touching only its own ticket's non-rail paths exits 0; a completed ticket's rails are inert; the #228 version-only exemption and sanctioned additions behave exactly as before; `--record` unchanged.
5. Agreement with CI: a test drives BOTH the local bin (`--ticket mine`) and `runRailFreezeGate` from lib/ci/rail-freeze.mjs over the SAME fixture repo and diff (one active ticket `mine`, one active ticket `other` with a rail, one completed ticket with a rail, a commit editing `other`'s rail) and asserts both verdicts are failures naming the same path, and that editing only the completed ticket's rail passes in both. Treat `runRailFreezeGate`'s argument shape as read-only.
6. Documentation: `packages/rails-guard/README.md` (flag table :37 and the rails-resolution rules :45-48) and by hand `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/rails-guard.mdx` (:32, :39): rails are the union of every active ticket's declarations; `--ticket` selects suppression allowances and the reported id; a violation names the owning ticket.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 Editing another active ticket's rail with `--ticket mine` → exit 2, human output names the path, the glob and `(rail of ticket <other>)`, JSON violation carries `ownerTicket: '<other>'`. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/rails-union.test.mjs`
- AC2 Same fixture, a change only to `mine`'s non-rail path → exit 0; a change only to the completed ticket's railed path → exit 0 (rails inert). verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/rails-union.test.mjs`
- AC3 No `--ticket` and no `--rails` → legal; the union is checked; a rail edit exits 2 with the owner named; with no active rails at all → exit 1 with the new message. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/rails-union.test.mjs`
- AC4 `resolveRailSet` table: cli globs win with owner null; completed tickets excluded only on strict `true` (`'true'`, `1` do not exclude); duplicates collapse; inputs not mutated. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/rails-union.test.mjs`
- AC5 Local verdict and `runRailFreezeGate` agree on the two diffs of normative item 5. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/rails-union.test.mjs`
- AC6 Existing suite green; tests that asserted the old `--ticket`-only resolution or the old no-ticket error text are rewritten and named in the PR body. verify: `npm test -w packages/rails-guard`
- AC7 Docs updated in both places. verify: `grep -c "owning ticket" packages/rails-guard/README.md apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/rails-guard.mdx` (each >= 1)
- AC8 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)
- AC9 `node packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs tier-check --author-provider anthropic --base origin/main` run in the worktree after the final commit reports TRUST-ROOT and prints the `git-change:<base>:<digest>` string; it is quoted verbatim in the PR body for the attestation ceremony. verify: the command above

OUT OF SCOPE: lib/ci/** (CI already takes the union), the PreToolUse plugin hooks (they read the active ticket by design), tier.mjs, the suppression marker grammar, #740/#741 (README flag docs beyond the lines named above).
title: rails-guard: the local gate checks the union of every active ticket's rails and names the owning ticket
